title: Modeling the CNOT gate in Germanium double quantum dots
abstract: We model a controlled-NOT (CNOT) gate mediated by exchange interactions in a realistic Ge/GeSi hole spin-qubit device. We use for that purpose a computationally efficient framework based on a compact dressed basis of many-body singlet and triplet states, which enables fast time-dependent simulations that would be prohibitive within a conventional configuration-interaction approach. We discuss the dominant sources of infidelity in ideal (noise-free) devices. On the one hand, the nonadiabaticity of the tunnel barrier ramps, enhanced by the transverse component of the exchange interaction, imposes limits on the speed of the CNOT gate. On the other hand, the AC Stark shift of the conditional resonance and the off-resonant driving of the complementary transition can significantly degrade the gate fidelity and call for a careful optimization of the driving conditions. Finally, we investigate the impact of quasi-static charge noise on the fidelity of the CNOT gate. We find that the capture of charges near the qubits can strongly disrupt the conditional operation, while the nanometer-scale motion of charges results in a loss of fidelity that sensitively depends on the position and strength of the corresponding dipole. Our results quantify the requirements on barrier control, microwave driving, and charge-noise stability for high-fidelity two-qubit operations in Ge/GeSi hole-spin qubits.
summary: This work theoretically models the CNOT gate operation in hole spin qubits within a Germanium double quantum dot. It identifies key sources of gate infidelity, including non-adiabatic dynamics and charge noise effects. The results quantify the necessary control over barrier ramps and microwave driving to achieve high-fidelity quantum operations.
main_problem: The paper models and analyzes the sources of infidelity when implementing a Controlled-NOT (CNOT) gate using hole spin qubits in a Germanium double quantum dot.
main_result: Infidelity is limited by non-adiabaticity during barrier ramps, the AC Stark shift of the conditional resonance, and the disruptive effects of charge noise (both static capture and dynamic motion).
method: Time-dependent simulations are performed using a computationally efficient dressed basis approach to track the evolution of the spin system through the gate sequence.
model_or_system: The system is a hole spin-qubit device in a Ge/GeSi DQD, modeled by an effective Hamiltonian involving longitudinal and transverse exchange interactions ($J_{\parallel}, J_{\perp}$) and Zeeman splitting. The CNOT gate relies on resonant microwave driving conditional on the state of one qubit.
key_observables: Gate fidelity ($F$), probability of leakage outside the computational subspace, and the dependence of fidelity on noise parameters.
important_parameters: Tunnel coupling ($J$), microwave driving frequency ($f_{\downarrow}$), barrier ramp speed ($	au_J$), and charge noise dipole moment ($p=qd$).
main_assumptions: The use of a compact dressed basis set is necessary to manage the computational cost compared to a full Configuration Interaction approach.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the DQD device structure, the energy level scheme for relevant transitions, and probability distributions showing state evolution during gate ramps.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the physical model and the CNOT protocol, then analyzes ideal limitations (non-adiabaticity, Stark shifts), and finally quantifies the impact of charge noise on the gate fidelity.
why_interesting: It provides quantitative metrics for realizing high-fidelity two-qubit gates in solid-state spin qubits, directly addressing the engineering challenges of noise and control required for quantum computation.
